newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GENERALE BANK JUMPS ON BBL MERGER COMMENT.
newsitem.headline: GENERALE BANK JUMPS ON BBL MERGER COMMENT.

text.p: Shares in Belgium's biggest bank Generale Bank surged more than four percent on Monday as its chief shareholder again reiterated it would support a merger with domestic rival BBL .

Around 1100 GMT, Generale Bank -- which is due to release full-year 1996 earnings figures on Tuesday -- was up 550 francs, or 4.20 percent at 13,650 francs. The shares set a new all-time high of 13,675 francs earlier when the merger news broke.

The chief executive officer or Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) , which owns 29 percent of Generale Bank, was quoted on Monday as saying he would still like a merger with BBL.
His comment in the magazine of the Flemish Investment Club Federation VFB came one week after BBL said at its annual results news conference it was for now pursuing a "stand alone" policy.
"One bank says one thing; the other something else...I think we are reaching selling levels (in the share), but no one wants to be caught short if there is a merger," one trader said.
BBL's share was up 100 francs, or 1.24 percent, at 8,190.
The market has been rife with the BBL merger story since August 1995 when the bank's then chief executive officer Daniel Cardon de Lichtbuer said he would like to conclude an alliance in 1996.

A link with Generale Bank was mooted, but was blocked by Internationale Nederlanden Groep , BBL's biggest shareholder. Dutch ING failed itself to buy BBL in 1992 when it offered 3,600 francs for its shares.
One trader noted that if ING sold now it would make a handsome profit on its stake.
"There has been market talk that seven Generale Bank shares would be offered for 10 BBL, which would value BBL at more than 9,000 francs. But there are always rumours," the trader added.
He said he himself did not see the logic of a link up. "If a big Belgian bank merges it should do it with a foreign partner," he said.
